quests.question: ___ that the risks were significant, the expedition team decided to proceed.
quests.hint: This very formal phrase introduces a concession, suited to legal or official writing.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite the significant risks, the team proceeded.

quests.question: The plan succeeded ___ early sales exceeded every internal projection.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the plan's success extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the success is measured specifically by this sales result.

quests.question: The strategy looked sound on paper, ___ execution proved far more difficult.
quests.hint: A good plan still ran into real-world difficulty.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a sound plan still faced execution problems.

quests.question: ___ the funding cut, the project would collapse within months.
quests.hint: Look closely at the verb form right after the blank — only one of these four options matches it.
quests.explanation: 'Were' inverts a hypothetical condition without 'if' — 'were the funding cut' matches 'would collapse'. 'Had' would need 'been cut'; 'should' would need 'be cut'.

quests.question: The previous CEO focused on cost-cutting, ___ the new one is investing heavily in growth.
quests.hint: Two leadership approaches are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two CEOs with two different strategies.

quests.question: Shareholders demanded a review ___ quarterly losses had tripled.
quests.hint: A financial result explains the demand.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a demand — tripled losses caused shareholders to act.

quests.question: ___ difficult was the exam that half the class failed.
quests.hint: This word pairs with an adjective and can trigger inverted word order when placed first.
quests.explanation: 'So' combines with an adjective to trigger inversion when fronted — 'so difficult was the exam' reverses the normal subject-verb order.

quests.question: The findings are reliable ___ the sample represents the wider population accurately.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the reliability extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the reliability depends specifically on this representative sample.

quests.question: ___ peer review takes months, publication delays are common in this field.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for explaining a common pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for an outcome — the slow review process explains the delays.

quests.question: ___ has the treatment reduced symptoms, but it has also shortened recovery time.
quests.hint: Placed first in the sentence, this phrase forces the subject and helper verb to swap places.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' at the front of a sentence triggers inversion — here matched with 'has' for the present perfect tense.

quests.question: The first trial tested a single dose, ___ the second trial compares multiple dosages.
quests.hint: Two trials are being placed side by side in contrast.
quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two trials with two different designs.

quests.question: The trial was halted early ___ the results were unambiguously positive.
quests.hint: A strong result explains an early decision.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — clearly positive results caused the early stop.

quests.question: ___ that costs would rise, the ministry expanded free screening to every region.
quests.hint: This very formal phrase introduces a concession, suited to legal or official writing.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite rising costs, the ministry expanded the program.

quests.question: The new therapy helps ___ patients report fewer relapses within the first year.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the therapy's benefit extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — the benefit is measured specifically by fewer relapses.

quests.question: The diagnosis was devastating news, ___ the family found reasons for hope in the treatment options.

quests.explanation: 'Yet' shows surprising contrast — devastating news still allowed for hope.

quests.question: ___ the team tested the software more thoroughly, they would have caught the bug.

quests.explanation: 'Had' inverts a past hypothetical condition without 'if' — 'had tested' matches 'would have caught' in the same past-hypothetical tense.

quests.question: The beta version crashed frequently, ___ the final release has proven remarkably stable.

quests.explanation: 'While' can contrast two related facts — two versions with two different stability records.

quests.question: Engineers added redundant servers ___ a single failure wouldn't take the whole system down.

quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose — redundant servers were added to prevent total failure.

quests.question: ___ more data the model receives, ___ more accurate its predictions become.
quests.hint: This pattern matches one increasing degree to another, in parallel.
quests.explanation: 'The...the' shows that one increase causes a matching increase — more data leads to more accuracy.

quests.question: The system is secure ___ every access request is independently verified.

quests.question: The migration was postponed ___ the backup system hadn't been fully tested.

quests.question: ___ the flight be delayed, passengers will be notified by text message.
quests.hint: The exact verb form after the blank narrows this down to just one grammatically correct choice.
quests.explanation: 'Should' inverts a possible future condition without 'if' — 'should the flight be delayed' matches the base verb form given here.

quests.question: Budget airlines charge separately for luggage, ___ full-service carriers usually include it.

quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two pricing models used by two types of airlines.

quests.question: The airline offered a generous refund, ___ many passengers had already booked alternative flights.

quests.question: ___ that the case was complex, the jury reached a verdict within two days.

quests.question: ___ both parties had signed the agreement, the court upheld its terms.

quests.question: The clause was added ___ both parties would be protected from unexpected costs.

quests.question: ___ did the ruling clarify the law, but it also set a precedent for future cases.
quests.hint: This opening phrase is the only one of the four that flips the normal subject-verb order.

quests.question: Civil cases require a lower burden of proof, ___ criminal cases demand proof beyond reasonable doubt.

quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two different standards used in two types of cases.

quests.question: The ruling applies ___ similar cases share the same specific circumstances.

quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the ruling's reach is limited to this specific condition.
